subject.title: Feature: --agent flag for TUI to select which agent handles the session

question: Should `openclaw tui` add a public `--agent <id>` startup selector, with the flag overriding cwd inference and conflicting agent-scoped `--session` values rejected?
rationale: The capability gap and implementation boundary are clear, but the precedence and conflict behavior alter the public TUI startup contract and require maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit selector
options.body: Add `--agent <id>`, let it override cwd inference, and reject a conflicting agent-scoped `--session` so one agent unambiguously owns startup.

options.title: Keep existing paths
options.body: Retain canonical agent-scoped session keys, workspace inference, remembered state, and post-launch switching without adding another public flag.

recommendation.title: Add explicit selector
recommendation.body: Add `--agent <id>`, let it override cwd inference, and reject a conflicting agent-scoped `--session` so one agent unambiguously owns startup.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently assessed this exact product gap and have broad historical involvement in the affected TUI surface.
